relations.subject: n1ql:unnest
relations.evidence: The `UNNEST` clause is used within the [FROM](from.md) clause.

relations.subject: n1ql:unnest
relations.evidence: To return the position of the elements in an unnested array after you use `UNNEST`, use the [UNNEST\_POS function](metafun.md#unnest-pos).

relations.subject: n1ql:unnest
relations.evidence: If you want to use an [ARRAY index](indexing-arrays.md) for the UNNEST query, you can use any arbitrary alias for the right side of the UNNEST — the alias does not have to be the same as the ARRAY index variable name in order to use that index.

notable_absence.finding: No access-control content - UNNEST is a FROM-clause term, not a statement in its own right, so it carries no independent RBAC gate; the underlying SELECT statement's privilege requirements (documented on comma.json/selectintro-type pages) govern access instead.
